does_not_prove.statement: The result holds for the controller revision (as declared by the caller; 'unstated' if none was declared), the contract draft versions and the reason registry named in subject.pinned. It does not carry to any other revision.

No claim that a decision was correct, that a policy was adequate, or that a grant was lawfully issued. The verifier checks structure, identity and agreement between records, not whether the decisions were right.

Destination checks cover only the rows in the supplied ledger snapshot. The snapshot has no sequence number, chain or signature, so completeness is not established: a dropped tail or a decision that never reached the ledger cannot be seen.

A forged set of records in which every commitment was recomputed to agree is indistinguishable from a genuine one by these checks. Agreement between records is not evidence that they are genuine. An intact journal (counts, order and bindings agree) does not show that any row was durably stored or retained: durable inclusion is not a level this verifier checks.
This is a verification report about supplied records. It is not signed, not an attestation, and authorizes nothing.
An input the strict parser refuses (duplicate members, NaN or Infinity, non-UTF-8, over-size, lone surrogates) is refused and reported, never repaired and re-read.
No claim about the scope or release status of any V1 of the stack. Nothing here is a release, a publication or an endorsement.
Agreement with a reference validator on a fixture set is a check against common-mode error. It does not show that the two implementations are equivalent.

x-notes: identity and ledger checks apply to control-plane run records only; this document kind has none
